title: ERIS vs Odoo
content_html:
ERIS vs Odoo compares two different ideas of business software. According to its website, Odoo is a suite of open source business apps for CRM, eCommerce, accounting, inventory, point of sale and project management. It has a free Community edition, and you can host it yourself or on Odoo's own hosting. ERIS from Upward Technologies (upwardtech.nl) is in beta now and starts from a different idea: one system for a company's business tools, with an AI assistant that answers from the company's own data and always uses a local AI model. ERIS runs on the company's own servers or is hosted for you by a cloud or telecom provider, also as a private cloud at a European provider. Odoo fits if you want open source code above all. Pick ERIS if your main concern is keeping company data away from outside AI providers while one AI assistant works across your business.

Status: ERIS is in beta now, with design partners. New apps arrive almost every week.

What Odoo is good at

Odoo covers a wide range of business tasks, and it gives you real choice over where it runs. The points below come from its website, read in November 2026.

  • A wide set of apps. Odoo describes itself as a suite of open source business apps "that cover all your company needs". It names CRM, eCommerce, accounting, inventory, point of sale and project management.
  • A free open source edition. Odoo comes in two editions. Community is open source and free. Enterprise adds extra apps, infrastructure and professional services.
  • You own your data format. Odoo stores data in PostgreSQL (an open source database). Its website says customers get the source code and GitHub access.
  • A choice of where it runs. The Standard plan is hosted on Odoo Online. The Custom plan lets you download Odoo Enterprise and host it yourself.
  • Support included in the plans. Odoo says all its plans include unlimited support, hosting and maintenance.
  • Separate data and backups. Each customer's data sits in its own database that is not shared with other customers. Odoo says it makes daily backups on two continents and copies them to at least 3 different data centres.
  • A security programme. Odoo says it takes part in CSA STAR Level 1 (the Cloud Security Alliance's Security Trust Assurance and Risk programme).

For a company that wants a broad, proven suite with open code, that is a strong offer.

What ERIS does differently

ERIS is built around the AI assistant and around where the AI runs. The points below describe what ERIS does.

  • One AI assistant across the business. The ERIS Assistant works across all apps on the company's own data, not inside one tool at a time.
  • A local AI model in both setups. ERIS uses a local AI model by default, whether it runs on your own servers or in the cloud. No outside AI provider receives client data in either setup.
  • Two ways to run it. You can run ERIS on your own servers or have Upward host it on its own servers in the Netherlands. With the on-premise option, the data never leaves your building.
  • Answers follow permissions. The assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open. If it refuses access, it logs that refusal like any other question.
  • Every AI action is logged. ERIS records who asked, which data was used, what the AI did and the result.
  • Instructions in documents stay content. The assistant reads instructions inside an email or document as content, never as commands to follow. This lowers the risk of prompt injection (hidden instructions meant to steer an AI).
  • One licence and one price per user. All standard apps are included. Custom apps, agents and knowledge bases are billed as projects.

Whether a setup meets GDPR (the EU data protection rules), NIS2 (the EU cybersecurity rules), DORA (the EU rules on digital resilience in finance) or the EU AI Act depends on the use case. That is checked for each deployment.

ERIS brings it all together in one system: meetings, meeting notes with a note taker, the task manager, project management, document management, document signing, CRM, bookkeeping, tax and procurement, standards (ISO 27001, NIS2), pipeline, quotes and outreach, content and social media, finance, HR, support and legal, all in the main portal with the ERIS Assistant, team chat and email.

Running it on your own servers: what to expect

Both products can run on your own hardware, but they ask for different things.

Odoo's self-hosted path is the Custom plan, where you download Odoo Enterprise and host it yourself. ERIS adds a local AI model on top of the business software. Local AI needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU (graphics processing unit) server. Its speed depends on that hardware, and your existing servers are not always enough. Running it yourself also costs hardware, maintenance and updates. The local model reads and searches company documents. It is not trained on them.

For installations that run offline, Upward Technologies uses this update path. Upward sends the update to the client through a sandbox, and the client installs it on its own servers. Each user's seat then installs the update from the client's server.

On maintenance, Upward's owner disagrees with the usual advice that on-premise software brings a heavy IT burden: "I have had multiple servers for 10 years and did not have much maintenance at all. Isn't that what IT is for?" A company that does not want to run its own hardware can choose the setup that Upward hosts on its own servers in the Netherlands.

For more on what on-premise AI involves, read how on-premises AI keeps enterprise data inside the firewall and what a local AI assistant for company documents takes.

Which one should you pick

  • You mainly want an eCommerce or point of sale suite. Odoo fits. Its website lists those apps.
  • You want open source code you can read and change, or a free starting point. Odoo fits. Its Community edition is open source and free, and its website says customers get the source code.
  • Your company cannot or will not send its data to an outside AI provider, and you want one AI assistant across your business tools. Pick ERIS. It runs a local AI model on your own servers or on Upward's own servers in the Netherlands, and logs every AI question and action.

If you are still comparing several suites, the guide to all-in-one business software covers more options. The ERIS vs Microsoft 365 Copilot comparison looks at the AI assistant side.

FAQ

What hardware do I need to run ERIS myself?

Local AI needs suitable hardware, usually a GPU server. How much you need depends on the AI models you choose. The ERIS pricing page has a calculator for working out the hardware for your company. Your existing servers are not always enough.

Can ERIS connect to my webshop, industry software or accountant?

Upward Technologies builds custom apps, agents and knowledge bases for a company as projects, and bills them separately. It also builds ERP and CRM integrations. Access is set per person, so the ERIS Assistant answers each person only from the data that person is allowed to open.

Is ERIS for a whole office or for one person on one computer?

ERIS runs for a whole company, either on its own hardware or hosted for you by a cloud or telecom provider, also as a private cloud at a European provider. According to its pricing page, a company with fewer than 10 staff can use a workstation of its own or Upward's server in the Netherlands.

How many users can ERIS have?

ERIS is priced as one licence and one price per user. The published pricing page sets the licence by company size, and the smallest companies pay per user only. There is no fixed limit on users.
